name: RichMessage
need: Rendering a chat message or an AI answer with structure (headings, quotes, code, lists, tables) is rebuilt wherever a model or a chat server talks to a user. teams-digest built it twice in one app: MessageBody renders typed blocks from the server, the inline Summary renders the digest's markdown-ish output. The safe pattern both converged on — typed shapes in, never HTML — is worth owning once.

consideredAlternatives.whyNot: A sanitiser is a guard on a door that should not exist; typed blocks make injection structurally impossible and keep the renderer 70 lines.
Full markdown is a bigger input language than any of our producers emit; the block contract is exactly what Teams and the digest actually send, and it stays inspectable.

proposedApi.RichMessage: blocks? (RichBlock[]: p | h | hr | quote | code | li | table), text (flat fallback, always present), className — inline marks **bold**, `code`, *em*; a wide table scrolls in its own container, never the page

sources: apps/teams-digest MessageBody (typed blocks from the server, 'nothing here ever receives HTML'), apps/teams-digest Summary (digest output rendering, same marks)
decision: Promote as a molecule (card surface); teams-digest adopts it for both call sites at its next feature touch (closing condition recorded in scout).
